column2: the planned stale-lock retry wraps only `commit()` / `commit_with_trailer()`, but production step 5 and stall-recovery paths hit `git add` before that wrapper runs. in `commit_main()`, `add_pathspec_file` / `add` execute first and return on failure when a stale `.git/index.lock` is present, so the guarded cleanup and retry never execute. the same gap exists on raw `git add --pathspec-from-file` in `_stage_and_commit_round` (step 5) and `commit_fixes --stage-all` (step 18a). recovery therefore still stalls on the lock until manual removal, matching the #4641 repro.

proposed stale-lock tests exercise `commit_main` without `--pathspec-from-file`, so they never hit `commit_main()`'s pre-commit `git add` gate. tests can pass while the production step 5 path (`--only --pathspec-from-file`, same shape as `_stage_and_commit_round` and `commit_fixes --stage-all`) still fails before any commit retry runs.

the plan deduplicates raw `git add` only in `_stage_and_commit_round` and `commit_fixes`, but leaves `_commit_lint_fix_delta_paths` with a standalone `git add` before `cli.py git commit`. step 5 post-round lint-fix commits can still fail on a stale `.git/index.lock` during the pre-commit add, stall as `lint-fix-commit-failed`, and never reach `git.py` lock policy or get distinct stale-lock cleanup/diagnostics.

changing `_stage_and_commit_round` to return `roundcommitresult` is not paired with an explicit test/migration update for existing monkeypatches. `test_apply_findings_with_coder_commit_failure_cleans_and_falls_through` still patches `_stage_and_commit_round` to return `str`; the new implementation can break or silently mis-route generic commit failures.

the plan removes raw `git add` from `commit_fixes` but does not update `scripts/test-implement-structure.sh`, which still requires `("git", "add", "--pathspec-from-file")` in `python/review_and_fix.py`. after deduping staging to `commit_main` only, `make lint` / the structure harness will fail even if the runtime change is correct.

python/review_and_fix.py:1162-1178 [scope-reduction] plan dedupes raw pre-add only in _stage_and_commit_round and commit_fixes but omits _commit_lint_fix_delta_paths. scenario: step 5 post-round lint-fix commits still call _run(["git", "add", "--pathspec-from-file", ...]) before cli.py git commit, bypassing git.py stale-lock sweep/retry; a 0-byte stale index.lock can still stall with lint-fix-commit-failed on the same execution path as the reported bug

introducing `stall_reason=stale-index-lock` while `stall_recovery.py` remains explicitly out of scope leaves step 18a unable to resume after an operator manually clears a lock larch conservatively refused to remove. `stale-index-lock` is not in `config.lint_fix_bail_reason_tokens`, `_classify_text` has no stale-lock branch, and evidence with lock diagnostics can fall through to `unrecoverable` with `resume_hint=none`, so `step5-review` is not dispatched even though the issue recovery contract expects a retryable path. by contrast, `coder-failed` stalls on step 5 can still classify as `transient-infra` and retain retry.

a `roundcommitresult` migration that changes `_stage_and_commit_round` without updating `apply_findings_with_coder` breaks failure handling. the call site still treats the return value as a string (`commit_sha = _stage_and_commit_round(...)`; `if not commit_sha:`). dataclass instances are always truthy, so `if not commit_sha` is always false. generic cleanup/fallback is skipped, and a non-`str` may be passed into `coderresult.commit_sha`.

python/git.py:46-54 planned `_has_live_git_process` scans for any system-wide git process instead of a repo-scoped or lock-holding check. scenario: operator runs `/design` or another git job in a different repo while a 0-byte stale `index.lock` blocks this repo; guarded removal is refused with `live git process detected` and step 5 / `commit_fixes --stage-all` still stall until manual `rm`
